intro: Executive assistants stay organized by shifting from reactive inbox management to a proactive triage system that categorizes tasks by impact and urgency. On a Mac, this requires a centralized capture strategy that pulls requests from email, Slack, and calendars into a single source of truth.
tldr: Adopt a triage mindset to sort tasks by impact rather than just speed.
Use a single, centralized tool to capture requests from all communication channels.
Align your deep work blocks with your executive's natural energy patterns.
Leverage Mac-native tools to reduce context switching and mental fatigue.

blocks.text: The reality of task prioritization for executive assistants

You are the gatekeeper for your executive. Every request feels urgent. The challenge is not just the volume of work but the constant re-sorting required when priorities shift. You might have 40 to 60 open items at any given moment. This creates decision fatigue. You end up exhausted from calculating what to do next rather than doing the work itself.
Why executive assistants struggle with project management

Most EAs fall into a cycle of reactive work. You clear the inbox, but you do not advance the project. Every request arrives with a label of urgent. This makes it hard to distinguish between a minor travel change and a board meeting preparation. You spend your day context switching. You move from email to Slack to calendar to document. Each switch costs you mental energy. This is called mental churn. It is more draining than the tasks themselves.
How to stay organized without buying new software

items: Use a single capture list. Do not rely on your memory or scattered flags in Outlook.
Implement a 10 minute reset pause. Every time your executive changes a priority, stop and re-evaluate your list.
Ruthlessly ignore low impact tasks. If a request does not move the needle for your executive, it can wait.
Align your work with your boss. Do your deep work when they are in meetings and unavailable.

faq.question: How do executive assistants stay organized when everything is urgent?
faq.answer: They use a triage system. Instead of treating all tasks as equal, they sort them by impact and ignore low priority items.

faq.question: What is the biggest productivity drain for EAs?
faq.answer: Constant context switching between different apps like email, Slack, and calendars causes mental churn.
